key_insight: The paper builds globally reliable, computable error estimators for monotone parametric nonlinear PDEs that can also be used directly as loss functions for neural network surrogates.
engineering_relevance: It enables certified training and assessment of physics-informed or operator-learning models by tying the loss value to the true solution error with explicit two-sided bounds.
method: Split the nonlinear operator into a linear residual plus a strongly monotone closure term.
Approximate the closure’s dual norm with a computable surrogate satisfying pairing and Lipschitz bounds.
Instantiate the framework for first-order system least-squares and discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin formulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical two-sided global bounds, verified assumptions for a model class of nonlinear fluxes, and explicit constants tracked over the parameter range.
watch_item: The approach depends on monotonicity and on constructing a surrogate dual norm that meets the required bounds, which may be nontrivial for more general nonlinearities or trial norms stronger than L2.
paper_title: Global error estimators for parametric monotone nonlinearities and neural approximations
